label: <DEL> or first-seen y/v/j/i/g in the input phase, boosted when the sequence starts with 1/p/o/f/q/0/z
explanation: Fires almost only in the input phase and at the delimiter (t=2..L). About half the activation mass is on <DEL>, but only 27% of <DEL> steps fire. The rest is on original-phase inputs, mostly a first occurrence of y (4.3x lift), v, j, i or g. Whether it fires depends on an interaction between the current input and the history: it is much more likely when the sequence starts with 1/p/o/f/q/0/z (2-2.6x lift), or when c/q/w/x/u appeared shortly before (prev2 lift ~2x). The current input set alone (<DEL> or first y/v/j/i/g, t>=2) reaches dev mass recall 0.80 but precision 0.27. Adding the first-token condition raises precision to 0.63 but drops recall to 0.38 (dev F1 0.47). The history dependence looks graded, like accumulated evidence, not a clean set rule. Does not fire at t=0, is rare at t=1, almost silent in the copy phase after the first output (copy share 4%), and weaker on repeated tokens (in_first=0 rate 1.3%). The top activations (~0.3) are on y, v and <DEL> in sequences that start with 1/o/q/f and contain c early. Not cleanly explained.
